The Indian Hotels Company Limited (IHCL), the Tata group hospitality company behind Taj, offers an attractive
combination of luxury brands, scarce hotel assets and a growing management-contract business. The operating
outlook remains healthy. The investment challenge is the price paid for that growth.
Our estimates imply roughly 16% annual growth in recurring attributable profit from FY26 to FY29. At the reference
price, investors pay about 53.6x FY27E and 45.9x FY28E recurring earnings. We see limited room for disappointment at

A brand platform with meaningful property exposure
IHCL combines three economic models. Owned hotels capture room and food-and-beverage revenue but require
substantial capital. Leased hotels reduce initial property investment while retaining rental obligations. Managed hotels
earn fees on properties funded by third-party owners, creating a more scalable source of profit.

IHCL shares for every 117 OHL shares held by eligible shareholders, excluding holdings that are cancelled under the
scheme. OHL has seven hotels and 825 rooms, with an important southern India presence.
